newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taipei sees chance for Taiwan-China summit.
newsitem.headline: Taipei sees chance for Taiwan-China summit.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday said two 1997 events in rival China -- Hong Kong's handover from Britain and a major Communist Party congress -- offered opportunity for a groundbreaking cross-straits leadership summit.

"After the Hong Kong handover or the 15th Communist Party congress when the Chinese communists' political transition is completed, this could be a chance for leaders from the sides to meet," said top China policymaker Chang King-yuh.
Chang, head of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, made the offer while briefing parliament on Taiwan-China relations, the state-funded Central News Agency reported.
Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui offered in 1996 to make a "journey of peace" to Beijing to meet President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin.

Taiwan is watching the mainland closely in the wake of the February 19 death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, assuming that his passing will severely test the supremacy of Jiang, Deng's hand-picked successor.
The Communist Party's 15th congress in October will be watched for changes in China's post-Deng leadership.
Chang's comment apparently came before a Chinese foreign ministry spokesman in Beijing reiterated China's determination not to restart semi-official talks frozen since June 1995.
Chinese spokesman Tang Guoqiang said such talks could be resumed only if Taiwan authorities "stop engaging in activities splitting the motherland".
China and Taiwan split after a civil war ended in 1949.
Jiang used his eulogy of Deng on Tuesday to issue his strongest call to date for Taiwan's reunification.
Beijing regards Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a rebel-held province and vows force to thwart any move toward independence. Taiwan advocates reunion, but only with a democratic mainland.

Taiwan flatly rejects reunification under Deng's "one country, two systems" model, which is being pioneered for Hong Kong's return to Chinese sovereignty in July after more than 150 years as a British colony.
China-Taiwan ties, never cordial, soured after Lee made a private but high-profile June 1995 trip to the United States.

Assailing the trip as promoting Taiwan's independence, Beijing froze semi-official talks and mounted eight months of war games and missile tests in what it ackowledged was a warning to Taiwan not to stray from the path of reunification.
